claims.claim: onsemi unveiled its Embedded Power Platform on September 16, 2026, using the silicon wafer itself as the package and targeting automotive, industrial and AI data-center power delivery.
The company states EPP can deliver 3-5x higher power density than current solutions by jointly optimizing electrical, mechanical and thermal design.

factors.name: AI infrastructure power-density exposure
factors.basis: EPP directly targets AI data-center power delivery where rack and board power density are increasing.

factors.name: architecture differentiation
factors.basis: Wafer-as-package integration is a materially different packaging architecture rather than an incremental discrete-component refresh.

risks.risk: Product announcement does not establish customer adoption, production scale, yield, pricing or economic returns.

unknowns.unknown: Named customers, production ramp timing and revenue contribution for EPP are not established in the cited release.

claims.claim: onsemi used its September 16 Investor Day to frame power, sensing and intelligent systems as the focused strategy across automotive, industrial and AI data centers.
EPP is a concrete technology release, but commercial execution remains to be demonstrated through qualification, production and customer adoption.

factors.name: strategy-product alignment
factors.basis: Investor Day strategic priorities and the EPP launch align around high-value power and AI infrastructure markets.

factors.name: expectation conversion
factors.basis: Technical density claims are promising but require commercial proof.

risks.risk: AI data-center exposure can become expectation-heavy before meaningful revenue is visible.

unknowns.unknown: No Scout valuation or numeric underwriting conclusion is asserted.
